{{Short description|Canadian mathematician and philosopher}}
{{for|the American surveyor of Omaha, Nebraska|William Newton Byers}}
'''William Paul Byers''' (born 1943) is a [[Canadian]] mathematician and philosopher; professor emeritus in mathematics and statistics at [[Concordia University (Quebec)|Concordia University]] in [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]], Canada.

He completed a BSc ('64), and an MSc ('65) from [[McGill University]], and obtained his PhD ('69) from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. His dissertation, ''Anosov Flows'', was supervised by [[Stephen Smale]].{{r|mg}}

His area of interests include [[dynamical system]]s and the [[philosophy of mathematics]].

==Books==
Byers is the author of three books on mathematics:
*''How Mathematicians Think: Using Ambiguity, Contradiction, and Paradox to Create Mathematics'' (Princeton University Press, 2007){{r|hmt}}
*''The Blind Spot: Science and the Crisis of Uncertainty'' (Princeton University Press, 2011){{r|bs}}
*''Deep Thinking: What Mathematics Can Teach Us About the Mind'' (World Scientific, 2015){{r|dt}}
